notes.title: Commandos: Origins Sets Course for Last Gen Consoles this September
notes.content:
[h1]Commandos: Origins Sets Course for Last Gen Consoles this September [/h1][p][/p][p]Publisher Kalypso Media and Claymore Game Studios announce that [b]Commandos: Origins will launch digitally on Xbox One and PlayStation®4 on September 17th, 2025[/b]. Following the release on PC (Steam and Epic Games), Xbox on PC, Xbox Series X|S, and PlayStation®5 in April, the game is now heading to last-gen consoles — inviting even more players to experience the thrilling origins of the legendary Commandos unit.   “We know that many of our fans have been with the Commandos series for decades — and a significant number of them are still playing on Xbox One and PlayStation 4,” said Jürgen Reusswig, Studio Director at Claymore Game Studios. “By bringing Commandos: Origins to last-gen consoles, we're honoring that legacy and making sure no one gets left behind.”   [/p][p]Commandos: Origins invites players to step back into World War II and command a squad of unique specialists through daring missions behind enemy lines. Designed with meticulous attention to detail, the game brings the series' iconic real-time tactics gameplay to life with modern enhancements — now optimized for the Xbox One and PlayStation 4 with all features from the current gen version. Whether sneaking past enemy patrols or blowing up strategic targets, last-gen players will be more than ready to show they still have what it takes.   [/p][p][b]Commandos: Origins is gearing up for digital release on Xbox One and PlayStation 4 on September 17, 2025, priced at €59.99 |£59.99 | $49.99[/b]. The Xbox One version supports Xbox Smart Delivery, ensuring players enjoy the best possible experience on both Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S — because no Commando leaves a comrade behind, not even across console generations. Commandos: Origins is available with Xbox Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass.  [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682441/0e86ee25775527af6314f70d4a01476225e6ecf6.jpg"][/img][/p][h3]Features:   [/h3][list][*][p][b]Challenging Real Time Tactical Stealth Gameplay[/b]: Make the best use of your Commandos’ unique abilities, infiltrate enemy facilities, and hit them where it hurts most before disappearing into the shadows.  [/p][/*][*][p][b]An extraordinary team[/b]: Featuring 6 infamous characters, each with their own storied history, banding together to form an extraordinary fighting force – the Commandos: Take control over Jack O’Hara “the Green Beret”, Thomas “the Sapper” Hancock, Francis T. “the Sniper” Woolridge, Samuel “the Driver” Brooklyn, James “the Marine” Blackwood, and Rene “the Spy” Duchamp and lead them to success.  [/p][/*][*][p][b]Many paths to victory[/b]: The detailed, varied, and interactive environments offer multiple approaches to reach your goal. Sneak, climb, drive in various vehicles, or hide and creep your way to mission success! [/p][/*][*][p][b]On your mark[/b]: A modern user experience with precise and intuitive controls enables you to control the commandos with expert precision. Coordinate complex actions simultaneously to overcome heavily fortified targets.  [/p][/*][*][p][b]Fight on all fronts[/b]: Play through more than 10 missions in historically authentic WWII environments, spanning from the barren Arctic to the African desert, with a range of core and voluntary objectives that will require your full tactical expertise. [/p][/*][*][p][b]There is no I in team[/b]: Take on missions with a friend in the 2-player cooperative multiplayer mode, either online or via local split-screen. 
[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Commandos: Origins – Deluxe Edition Marches onto Store Shelves
notes.content:
[h1]Commandos: Origins – Deluxe Edition Marches onto Store Shelves [/h1]

[h3]A special physical release created for loyal fans [/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682441/68bdb56c597f0aec43f90b18b18fc49a64beda62.jpg[/img]
 
We are proud to announce that the physical version of the Commandos: Origins – Deluxe Edition is now available at retail and online stores! Published across Germany, Austria, and Switzerland for Steam, Xbox Series X|S, and PlayStation®5 for €49.99|€59.99, as well as in the UK, selected EU territories and in the US on Xbox Series X|S and PlayStation 5 for £54.99/€59.99/$59.99, the Green Beret and his Commandos squad have now marched onto store shelves. The US version will release on June 24.

notes.content:
[h1]Commandos: Origins – Update 1.2[/h1]

[i]Commandos![/i]

[b]We've just released Update 1.2[/b] for Steam and all available platforms, which includes many more fixes for reported mission-specific issues, gameplay issues and crashes.
Update 1.2 for Commandos: Origins also contains some [b]implemented feedback[/b], like a new hotkey to select all Commandos and the option to turn off white movement lines for movement commands.

[u]For more details, please check out the full changelog below.[/u]

[i]Consider it done![/i]

[h3]Table of Content[/h3]
1) Additions/Adjustments

3) Mission-Specific Fixes 
4) Multiplayer Fixes 
5) UI/Settings Fixes 
6) Other Fixes

[*] Added: Achievements - New icons in Mission Selection Screen displaying if each mission was successfully finished by meeting the “Knock them out with kindness” and “No stone left unkilled” requirements. [*] Added: New Hotkey to select all Commandos which is customizable in the settings.[/list]

[list][*] Fixed: A random crash when moving 4 Commandos into a hiding location.
[*] Fixed: A random crash when killing an enemy.
[*] Fixed: A random crash when performing a melee attack.
[*] Fixed: A random crash when an enemy is searching for his missing conversation partner.
[*] Fixed: Crash – A crash in multiplayer in Operation Nightfall for the joining player when the host sabotages the water supply.
[*] Fixed: Crashes – 20 further rare cases of crashes reported by players.[/list]

[h3]3) Mission-Specific Fixes[/h3]
[list][*] Fixed: Operation Daybreak (Mission 1) – Optional objective of rescuing British soldiers sometimes displaying 5/3 instead of 3/3 upon completion.
[*] Fixed: Operation Falchion (Mission 2) – White noise sound effect of radio equipment in barracks not disappearing when transmitter gets turned off.
[*] Fixed: Operation Nightfall (Mission 3) – Optional objectives “Sabotage the vehicles fleet” and “sabotage the MG nests” showing 1/2 instead of 2/2 upon completion.

[*] Fixed: Operation Blindfold (Mission 6) – Cleared up the task structure to make clear that you need to destroy both radar stations OR 3 FLAKs in order to proceed with the mission.
[*] Fixed: Operation Blindfold (Mission 6) – Sometimes getting stuck after exiting truck.
[*] Fixed: Operation Blindfold (Mission 6) – Unable to use shovel in an area where it should be possible.
[*] Fixed: Operation Blindfold (Mission 6) – Enemy clerk sometimes facing the wrong direction, making one of the puzzles a little easier than intended.
[*] Fixed: Operation Blindfold (Mission 6) – Some textures not loading correctly in the airstrike cutscene.
[*] Fixed: Operation Blindfold (Mission 6) – A specific MG crew member reacting inconsistently to the same lure.
[*] Fixed: Operation Magpie (Mission 7) – Edge case where Driver was unable to leave MG after interacting with it.
[*] Fixed: Operation Trident (Mission 8) – The objective marker for cut communications sometimes missing after loading a save game.
[*] Fixed: Operation Trident (Mission 8) – Not being able to exit zodiac anywhere you can enter it from.
[*] Fixed: Operation Trident (Mission 8) – Some boats not having collision boxes, allowing the zodiac to pass through them.
[*] Fixed: Operation Aries (Mission 9) – Crew of the HMS sometimes getting stuck, preventing the player from finishing the mission.
[*] Fixed: Operation Aries (Mission 9) – Mission objective sometimes not updating correctly after destroying the naval gun, preventing the player from finishing the mission.
[*] Fixed: Operation Aries (Mission 9) – New soldiers arriving after incoming ship cutscene not getting displayed on minimap until saving & loading once.
[*] Fixed: Operation Aries (Mission 9) – Upper floor of an office building still getting displayed when it should not.
[*] Fixed: Operation Aries (Mission 9) – The open gate and the crashed ship not being visible on minimap after the incoming ship cutscene.
[*] Fixed: Operation Aries (Mission 9) – A wall not being displayed as destroyed after the incoming ship cutscene.
[*] Fixed: Operation Harbinger (Mission 10) – Hangar roof not disappearing automatically when approaching a specific side entrance door.

[*] Fixed: An edge case breaking the sound decoy for the rest of the mission upon loading.
[*] Fixed: The marine being able to shoot his harpoon through walls when crawling.
[*] Fixed: An edge case where an enemy did not find a Commando when searching the hiding location with the Commando in it.
[*] Fixed: An edge case where enemies kept on shooting on empty hiding locations.
[*] Fixed: Patrol leaders sometimes keeping on searching when the other members of the patrol already moved back to their regular behavior.
[*] Fixed: Knocked out enemies sometimes sliding back to their original position upon loading.
[*] Fixed: Enemy view cones sometimes being able to pass through the sides of certain closed doors.
[*] Fixed: A few inconsistencies with view cones, for example, a fence blocking the view cone when it should not or vice versa.
[*] Fixed: Sapper sometimes getting stuck when dragging a body and encountering differences in height.
[*] Fixed: Knocked-out enemies who get revived sometimes not resuming their regular behavior and remaining at the position where they got revived.[/list]

[h3]7) Platform/Input Specific Fixes[/h3]
[list][*] (PC) Fixed: Tooltips not disappearing reliably when hovering over buttons.
[*] (PC) Fixed: Timer since last save not having a tooltip.
[*] (PC) Fixed: Trees sometimes changing textures unexpectantly when scrolling over the map.
[*] (PC) Fixed: Several issues with the “Commandos Classic” keyboard and mouse control scheme.
[*] (PC) Fixed: DLSS option getting greyed out when trying to activate it.

[*] (Controller) Fixed: First Aid Kit ability UI hint being out of bounds when selecting the ability and approaching an injured Commando.
[*] (Controller) Fixed: Mission Failed Screen – Savegames not being selected in the right order when scrolling down the list, making only some save games selectable from this screen.

[*] (Controller) Fixed: Closing tutorial windows sometimes also changing stance of Commando.[/list]

[h3]8) Localization Fixes[/h3]
[list][*] Fixed: Arabic – Name of person currently speaking not on the right side of the sentence in the subtitles.
[*] Fixed: French – Some voice lines playing in English when language setting is French.
[*] Fixed: Changed the falsely displayed age of the Green Beret and the Sniper to 31.

[*] Fixed: Some typos in various languages.

notes.content:
[h1]Commandos: Origins - Update 1.1[/h1]

[i]Commandos! [/i]

[i]Thank you for your constructive feedback, suggestions and reviews![/i]

[h2]Changes [/h2]
[h3]1) Performance Fixes [/h3]
[list][*] Fixed an issue where Pine trees had a significant performance impact. Maps with many pine trees like Operation Blindfold will now have improved performance. 
[*] Fixed: Big FPS drop in the mission accomplished cutscene of Operation Cleaver. [/list]
[h3]2) Crash Fixes [/h3]
[list][*] Fixed: A crash related to the frequent use of the Marine’s abilities. 
[*] Fixed: Rare Crash related to using command mode with multiple Commandos.

[*] Fixed: Operation Cleaver (4) - Rare crash when triggering the outro cutscene.

[list][*] Fixed: Mission Accomplished Screen - Display of wrong Commmandos. 
[*] Fixed: Mission Accomplished Screen - “Completion time” not calculated correctly. 
[*] Fixed: Mission Accomplished Screen – Map statistics not getting tracked correctly. 
[*] Fixed: Settings - Hud Scale option showing more than 100%. 
[*] Fixed: Settings - “Display control hints” not hiding all control hints when set to “off”. 
[*] Fixed: Settings - Portraits looking blurry when VFX graphics option is set to “low”. 
[*] Fixed: Settings - Options for “Display Indicators” being switched around. [/list]

[list][*] Adjusted: Decreased the size of the displayed version number in the bottom right.

[list][*] Fixed: Multiplayer – The joining player was not able to use pistol. 
[*] Fixed: Multiplayer - Saving while the joining player picks up an enemy could lead to the joining player not being able to pick up the body anymore after loading.

[*] Fixed: Enemy snipers sometimes calling an alarm just because of seeing footprints, which should not happen. 
[*] Fixed: Sapper’s bear trap getting stuck on metal staircases. 
[*] Fixed: Some shadows cutting off view cones when they should not, leading to view cones with weird gaps. 
[*] Fixed: Commandos pathfinding near stationary guns not always choosing the direct path. 
[*] Fixed: Improved aiming accuracy with a PAK. 
[*] Fixed: Improved aiming accuracy with FLAK 88. 
[*] Fixed: Missing details of the damaged state of stationary guns and some vehicles.  
[*] Fixed: Allied characters having a red dot on the minimap as if they were the enemy. 
[*] Fixed: Mouse cursor misalignment on certain surfaces. 
[*] Fixed: Cleaned up some occurrences of view cones getting displayed where they should not, for example because there are assets in the way, blocking the view. 
[*] Fixed: Some instances where the objective marker would be displayed after the objective was already completed when loading the game. 
[*] Fixed: Enemy clerks sometimes searching a hiding location from too far away instead of walking close to it first. 
[*] Fixed: Rare instances of enemies carrying two rifles. 
[*] Fixed: Controllers falsely vibrating during certain cutscenes. 
[*] Fixed: Commandos sometimes moving on their own after loading when playing with a controller.[/list]

As the release of [b]Commandos: Origins on April 9th[/b] draws another week closer, we have sent our spy behind development lines again to gather the latest intel for you.

It's a [b]brand-new feature[/b] in the Commandos series, offering completely new tactical opportunities by allowing players to[b] queue actions across multiple characters[/b]. One example of this is being able to kill two guards who can see each other, without needing to distract one of them first. notes.title: Commandos: Origins Dev Insights
notes.content:
[h1]Commandos: Origins – Infiltrating the Development [/h1]

[b]As we approach the release of Commandos: Origins on April 9th[/b], we take a look back at four key development topics — this time with Dev Insights into topics like AI and User Experience, among two others. 

This is [b]your chance to take a look over our shoulders[/b] and get a sneak peek from our journey. 

[h2]Optimization[/h2]
[b][u]Up first, we have insight into fine-tuning the gameplay experience based on your feedback and focusing on performance optimization.[/u][/b] Programmer Marina, who is also taking care of bugfixes & polishing, talks about the process: 

[i]“After receiving the Beta feedback, we teamed up with Level Design to focus on the key areas we wanted to improve. Working together like this allowed us to adjust the code quickly, making the gameplay smoother and more enjoyable.”[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682441/aa138d2490235abf51d35519ecc982a896ffd056.png[/img]

There would be nothing to polish though without the game world itself. Commandos: Origins builds and relies on expansive maps with a multitude of tactical options.  

[h2]Expansive Map Design[/h2]
[u][b]Up second in this week's Insight Series is a look into the expansive map design. [/b][/u]

[b]Commandos: Origins is all about multiple approaches[/b] and different opportunities in each mission. The Level Design and Game Design team has opted for a multi-layered mission experience and variety in the gameplay - all taking place on expansive maps!  

Missions by night, for example, require an exceptional stealth approach - [b]Game Designer Jana told us more[/b] about what's important and different in those missions: 

[i]“Using the cover of the night and stealth tactics go hand in hand. When we designed Night Missions, our goal was to reflect the advantages of the night. Our first point of action was to impair the enemy’s vision. By drastically reducing the distance they can see clearly in, we left more room for the Commandos to sneak through. However, we quickly noticed that due to the sheer size of our levels, this allowed players to simply outmaneuver the enemies. While this was certainly very stealth focused, it reduced the threat of our enemies too much. We wanted our Night Missions to play differently, but not easier. [/i]

[i]In the next step we experimented with sound, if enemies can’t see as well, maybe they are more alert to sound? While initially a nice idea, we scrapped it. We want our players to gradually master the Commando’s tools, and for that to work those tools need to be predictable. A gun does not suddenly emit more noise just because the sun has set. Eventually we brought light back into the mix. Equipping some enemies with flashlights allows them to see almost as well as during daytime. Still, we wanted something that clearly made Night Missions different. Our solution: Using stationary light sources as environmental obstacle. While light alone does no harm, it fully exposes Commandos in illuminated areas if an enemy looks in their direction. With all these systems in place, we hope players are encouraged to truly operate ‘from the shadows’.”  [/i]

[h3]The result of some of these design choices can be seen in our Dev Update Video:[/h3]
https://www.youtube.com/shorts/DCcWFW3vl4g



However, even the best and most carefully designed maps would be boring without smart enemies to challenge you. That’s where the AI comes in and takes a pivotal role in Commandos Origins. Let’s take a look into how the team tackles this essential gameplay part. 

[h2]Ai Behaviour[/h2]
[u][b]For the third topic on Dev Insights, the team shared their thoughts on tackling AI behaviour. [/b][/u]

[b]Mission tactics are critical[/b], so it is essential that enemies react logically to your actions and advance, which makes AI behaviour an essential gameplay aspect in Commandos: Origins.   

[b]Lead Programmer Rahul talked about the teams' workflow concerning AI:[/b] 

[i]“Using a dynamic system that allows designers to control AI behaviour at the time of level design, we ensure the AI behaves appropriately to the current situation in the mission. Our missions are meticulously designed, keeping in mind the design goals of the AI behaviour, finely balancing them with the goals of our level design to have a balanced difficulty, realistic challenges and intriguing puzzles.” [/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682441/995b0d8695ebb5e6efab73f1e951b2a212829140.jpg[/img]

Gameplay is not just what happens on screen though, but also how the game feels and how our players experience it. That is where User Experience comes in, which the Commandos: Origins Team constantly refined, shaped by player feedback directly. 
 
[h2]User Experience[/h2]
[u][b]Last but not least topic as our fourth dev insights topic Producer Moritz discusses feedback utilization for improving the game. [/b][/u]

[i]How do I move my Commando? What do I have to do now?[/i][i] Is anything breaking my immersion?[/i] The User Experience (UX) of Commandos: Origins combines simplicity with efficiency, guiding the player and enabling a smooth and immersive gameplay experience.  

Crafted by the Design and Art team and implemented by the Code team, it is constantly getting improved throughout the development process based on feedback from players playing the game.  

Our [b]Producer Moritz gave an example[/b] of how your feedback helped us improve the game. 

[i]“Seeing recordings of players experiencing the game for the first time helps massively in identifying issues we might have overlooked ourselves after working on this game until now. We sometimes know the game too well already to understand what players might miss at first try. Some players, for example, had issues finding out how to shoot barrels in the demo, initially you had to hold CTRL in order to shoot anything non-human. While this was mentioned in one of the tutorial hints, this crucial information was often overlooked. Therefore, we decided to make barrels targetable without holding CTRL, enabling a smoother user experience overall.” 
[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682441/e40341f8ce8a5944f496745de56ac1c283fe71a1.jpg[/img]

That wraps up this edition of our Dev Insights Series — giving you a[b] closer look at the work that went into Commandos: Origins[/b], and how the Team tackles essential parts like Map Design, AI Behavior, User Experience and Polishing behind the scenes.  

[b]We can’t wait for you to enjoy Commandos: Origins on release. [/b]

notes.title: Commandos: Origins FAQ
notes.content:
[h1]Commandos: Origins FAQ [/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682441/04c0d57021f6ed5f8330ce320766d48095c46106.png[/img]

[b]Genre:[/b] Real-Time-Tactics / Strategy 
[b]Release Date:[/b] Out now!
[h3]Age Rating[/h3]
[b]IARC Ratings:[/b]
[b]ESRB:[/b] Teen 
[b]PEGI:[/b] 16 

[b]Plattforms: [/b]
On Day One with Xbox Game Pass for console & PC with Xbox Game Pass, Windows PC, PlayStation®5 & Xbox Series X|S; 
Digital versions on Xbox One (including Xbox Smart Delivery) and PlayStation® 4 will launch later this year.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682441/98eee7cf0a53e0099b9133aac8dfcdc38d7e685c.png[/img]

[h2]What is Commandos: Origins? [/h2]

[b]Commandos: Origins[/b] is the long-awaited sequel to the Commandos series, taking you back to the roots of the real-time tactics genre. It delves into the days when Jack O’Hara – the Green Beret – and his five comrades became the infamous squad renowned for taking on missions no one else would dare attempt. 

YOU have been chosen for a special mission that will determine the fate of the world and give rise to this legendary elite unit. 

A new chapter awaits in the shadowy depths of World War II history, where heroes are born, and legends are forged. Whether for a daring raid, covert sabotage, or a heroic rescue mission, the Green Beret, the Engineer, the Sniper, the Driver, the Marine, and the Spy must combine their skills to accomplish their challenging objectives. Success will only come if you craft a thoughtful plan and cleverly combine targeted attacks with stealth maneuvers. 

From the icy plains of the Arctic to the vast deserts of Africa, from the western coasts of Europe to the Eastern Front, it’s up to you to lead the Commandos in high-stakes operations to combat the Nazi occupation and achieve victory. 

[h2]What are the core features of Commandos: Origins? [/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Challenging Real-Time Tactics and Stealth Gameplay:[/b] Use your Commandos' unique abilities to infiltrate enemy bases, strike at strategic points, and vanish back into the shadows. 
[*] [b]An Extraordinary Team:[/b] Six infamous characters, each with their own story, unite to form an exceptional task force – the Commandos. Take control of Jack O’Hara, the "Green Beret," Thomas "The Engineer" Hancock, Francis T. "The Sniper" Woolridge, Samuel "The Driver" Brooklyn, James "The Marine" Blackwood, and Rene "The Spy" Duchamp, and lead them to victory. 
[*] [b]Multiple Paths to Victory:[/b] Detailed, diverse, and interactive environments offer various ways to achieve your objectives. Hide, climb, drive different vehicles, or sneak and crawl your way to mission success! 
[*] [b]At Your Command:[/b] A modern gameplay experience with precise, intuitive controls lets you deploy your Commandos with pinpoint accuracy. Coordinate and execute multiple complex actions simultaneously to overcome heavily guarded objectives. 
[*] [b]Battle on All Fronts:[/b] Undertake over 10 missions at historically authentic World War II locations, from the barren Arctic to the African desert. Each mission includes numerous primary and optional objectives to challenge your tactical expertise. 
[*] [b]Teamwork:[/b] Tackle missions together with a friend in 2-player co-op multiplayer, either online or via local split-screen. [/list]

[h2]What is the difference of Commandos: Origins compared to the legacy Commandos games? [/h2]

[b]Commandos: Origins[/b] takes the complex tactical gameplay of the classic Commandos games to the next level.  

It features even larger maps, an isometric 3D real-time environment with zoom-in and rotation capabilities, and more interactions with the environment, such as the ability to use surroundings to eliminate enemies.  

These elements significantly enhance the replayability of the game. The combination of massive maps and various approaches to solving missions offers players a wide variety of tactical options and ensures each map remains engaging over multiple playthroughs.  

Additionally, multi-story buildings are now seamlessly integrated into the maps, removing the need to switch to a separate gameplay window. 

[h2]What is the core gameplay in Commandos: Origins? [/h2]

In [b]Commandos: Origins[/b], tactics are key. Use the Commandos' abilities to your strategic advantage—in real-time! Coordinate multiple complex actions and execute them simultaneously to reach heavily guarded objectives (Command Mode). 

Achieve your goal by navigating through detailed, diverse, and interactive environments, using stealth gameplay (daring, loud actions may get you ahead faster, but be prepared for a possible "ALARM!"). 

Pay attention to the various conditions of the map – on certain surfaces, the Commandos may leave footprints that enemies can detect. At night, the enemies' field of vision is smaller, but be careful. 

[h2]Are there one or multiple ways to complete a mission? [/h2]

In Commandos: Origins, there are multiple approaches to fulfill the mission objective – based on the available Commando units, their unique abilities and your preferences. It’s up to you to choose your path. 

[h2]How many missions does Commandos: Origins have? [/h2]

[b]Commandos: Origins[/b] has 14 missions, each featuring 1 to 2 unique objectives that appear only once in the game. Additionally, there are numerous side tasks to complete within the missions. 

[h2]How does the stealth system work in Commandos: Origins? [/h2]

In [b]Commandos: Origins[/b], both lethal and non-lethal enemy takedowns are possible. Dispose of enemies out of sight of others and avoid the enemy's line of sight. When you move while prone, enemies won't see you within the striped area of their vision cone. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682441/91494024ab174861f0813e1554e8b4bc3dd81923.png[/img]

[h2]Will there be a modern planning system in Commandos: Origins? [/h2]

To help you to strategically plan and execute your actions, we implemented the Command Mode: With this, you have the option to queue actions from your different Commando units so they can be performed simultaneously. 
 
[h2]Can you collect loot in Commandos: Origins? [/h2]

Yes, you can collect loot in [b]Commandos: Origins[/b]. Our modernized loot system aligns with our vision of staying true to the Commandos series’ core, prioritizing stealth rather than giving the player the ability to just blast into enemy territory. What does this mean for Commandos: Origins? Some enemies have ‘lootable’ items such as ammunition and first aid kits when they are eliminated or killed. You can also find loot, such as collectibles and uniforms, in certain locations in the environment. Once you pick up an item, this is directly available for the selected Commando via his abilities without needing an additional inventory (i.e. backpack).

[h2]Is there a way to adjust the difficulty in Commandos: Origins? [/h2]

Yes! In [b]Commandos: Origins[/b], you can choose from three difficulty levels: 

[b]Beginner:[/b] Suitable for recruits who are playing for the first time. You’ll learn how to approach scenarios with some room for mistakes. Enemies react more slowly, and your Commandos have more health. 

[b]Normal:[/b] Suitable for recruits who have experienced combat before. You know advanced strategies and have mastered various combat skills. Enemies react faster, and your Commandos can withstand a moderate amount of damage. 

[b]Hard:[/b] Only for veterans. You must plan and execute your actions perfectly on the battlefield. Enemies react immediately, and your Commandos have very limited health. 

[h2]Are there different enemy types in Commandos: Origins? [/h2]

In [b]Commandos: Origins[/b], there are multiple enemy types which have different traits. For example, Guards are usually stationed around locations of high tactical value. With their watchful eye and an MP40 at hand they are not to be underestimated. Guards will not move from their assigned post which makes entering the guarded area quite challenging. Officers, however, oversee the local forces and are often in charge of patrols, manning a Luger. 

It's on you to find the best tactics for each enemy! 

[h2]What role do environmental interactions play in Commandos: Origins? [/h2]

In [b]Commandos: Origins[/b], there are environmental takedowns and clues that you can collect, offering you additional and alternative ways to complete objectives. Additionally, you can collect items such as first aid kits, ammunition, enemy uniforms for the spy, and more from the environment. 

[h2]What vehicles will be available in Commandos: Origins? [/h2]

In [b]Commandos: Origins[/b], the following vehicles will be available: 
[list][*] Opel Blitz (4 variations) 
[*] Kübelwagen 
[*] Jeep Willys 
[*] Panzerkampfwagen 3 
[*] Zodiac boat (mission-specific) [/list]

Additionally, there are several stationary objects that can be used, such as the 50mm PAK 38, Flakvierling, Flak 88, or the MG34. 

[h2]On which platforms will Commandos: Origins be released? [/h2]

[b]Commandos: Origins[/b] will be available on Day One with Xbox Game Pass for console and PC, and will be released for Windows PC, Xbox Series X|S, and PlayStation®5! 

[h2]Will Commandos: Origins release on Xbox One and PlayStation 4? [/h2]

[b]Commandos: Origins[/b] will have digital versions for PlayStation® 4 and Xbox One that follow later this year. 

[h2]Will there be a Deluxe Edition of Commandos: Origins? [/h2]

[b]Commandos: Origins[/b] will feature a digital Standard Edition as well as a digital Deluxe Edition available on April 9th on Windows PC, PlayStation®5 and Xbox Series X|S. The physical edition will be available as Deluxe Edition on May 22nd (this might vary depending on the region you are buying from). 

[h3]The Deluxe Edition will include: [/h3]

[b]Legacy Skins:[/b] With this package, the 6 Commandos of Commandos: Origins can change their visuals to reflect the classic style of Commandos 2: Men of Courage.  

[b]Digital Calendar:[/b] With 12 unique motifs from the game, this digital calendar brings some Commandos spirit into your everyday life.  

[b]Original Soundtrack: [/b]Let the 15 carefully crafted symphonic tracks of the original soundtrack carry you away into the challenging WWII settings of the game. 

[b]Unique 3D-Print Template:[/b] Print your own Green Beret Bust with this exclusive 3D-Print Template. 

[h2]Will Commandos: Origins have a retail edition? [/h2]

[b]Commandos: Origins[/b] will have a retail edition for PC, PlayStation® 5 and Xbox Series X on May 22nd – this might vary depending on the region you are buying from. We’ll keep you updated! 

[h2]Will Commandos: Origins include a multiplayer mode? [/h2]

[b]Commandos: Origins[/b] will feature a 2-player multiplayer mode. The missions (except mission 1) will be playable in co-op mode, either online or via local split-screen. 

[h2]Will Commandos: Origins support modding? [/h2]

Mod support for[b] Commandos: Origins[/b] is currently not planned. 

[h2]How does the save system work in Commandos: Origins? [/h2]

In [b]Commandos: Origins[/b], there is the option to manually save the game or use the quick save feature. (PC: F5 for quicksave & F8 for quickload; Xbox: Press Select button once for quicksave & hold for quickload; PS5: press Touchpad for quicksave & hold Touchpad for quickload) 

[h2]What is the control system like in Commandos: Origins? [/h2]

In [b]Commandos: Origins[/b], you can either play with mouse and keyboard on PC or controller on PC, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. There will be multiple different control schemes to choose from and, for PC, we’re making custom key-binding available so you can adjust the controls to your liking. 

[h2]Who are the developers of Commandos: Origins? [/h2]

The developers of[b] Commandos: Origins[/b] are Claymore Game Studios. 

[h2]Which game engine is used for Commandos: Origins? [/h2]

[b]Commandos: Origins[/b] is being developed in the latest version of the Unreal Engine (Unreal Engine 5).

notes.title: Commandos: Origins - Brand New Trailer
notes.content:
[h1]Commandos: Origins Debuts Brand New Trailer[/h1]
[h2]A sneak peek into the fan-favorite real-time stealth tactics game[/h2]

Soldiers, embark on a mission to the very beginning... We have officially showcased new video footage of Commandos: Origins, the latest in the classic real-time stealth tactics game series. Join the front lines with iconic characters Jack O'Hara (The Green Beret) and Francis T. Woolridge (The Sniper) as they assemble the original Commandos force, leading the team through authentic historical locations during World War II.

[b]Get a first look of the diversity of maps with the Commandos: Origins GDC trailer:[/b]
[previewyoutube=BYyO_HrKdYY;full][/previewyoutube]
 
Experience the intensity of diverse map scenarios, from infiltrating enemy bases amidst the icy landscapes of the Arctic, to engaging in close quarters combat on a German submarine under the cover of night, to navigating the scorching sands of the African Desert.
 
"While designing the intended experience for Commandos: Origins, we kept a close eye on the history of the original games and on authenticity towards the World War II setting. Our missions are all inspired by real events, locations, and battles, and are designed for a wide variety of tactical approaches by the player. We know that fans of the franchise have high expectations for Commandos: Origins, and we try our best to live up to these expectations with our commitment to a worthwhile 'Commandos' experience," said Juergen Reusswig, Studio Director at Claymore Game Studios.

notes.title: Enlist as a Cadet for early access testing phases!
notes.content:
[h1]Enlist as a Cadet for early access testing phases![/h1]

Alarm! Alarm! Prepare to once again lace the boots of the legendary Commandos squad! 
[b]We are looking for aspiring Cadets to assist in the upcoming revival of the fan-favourite Commandos series in Commandos: Origins.[/b] War has once again found itself at the doorstep of the great powers with World War II, and only heroic deeds will be enough to fight against it. The development team are looking for both seasoned Commandos veterans and talented new cadets to help shape this new campaign.

Take part in several missions across varied locations, from the scorching African Desert to the unforgiving tundra of the Arctic. At the forefront of this gripping conflict is the Commandos led by Jack O'Hara, The Green Beret.

Can you report the latest intel to HQ? Will you forage for bugs in the jungle undergrowth? Are you a commando waiting for your origin? Enlist today as a Cadet for Commandos: Origins to be considered for [b]any upcoming PC Alphas/Betas across Steam and the Microsoft Store.[/b] If you are selected, you will receive an invitation via email to take part in the survey and which will direct you to an exclusive Discord server where you can give feedback directly to the developers.

[h3]ENLIST NOW:[/h3]
[url=https://kalypsomedia.com/playtest/commandos-origins/]https://kalypsomedia.com/playtest/commandos-origins/[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682441/1ddc328f2ad0a9a7dbd03063be9a6258f7aa8663.jpg[/img]

Commandos: Origins is gearing up for a 2024 release and will be available on day one with Xbox Game Pass for console and PC and on Xbox Series X|S, Windows PC, and PlayStation 5.

[h3]Features:[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Challenging Real Time Tactical Stealth Gameplay[/b]: Make the best use of your Commandos’ unique abilities, infiltrate enemy facilities and hit them where it hurts most before disappearing into the shadows.
[*] [b]An extraordinary team[/b]: Featuring 6 infamous characters, each with their own storied history, banding together to form an extraordinary fighting force – the Commandos: Take control over Jack O’Hara “the Green Beret”, Thomas “the Sapper” Hancock, Francis T. “the Sniper” Woolridge, Samuel “the Driver” Brooklyn, James “the Marine” Blackwood, and Rene “the Spy” Duchamp and lead them to success.
[*] [b]Many paths to victory[/b]: The detailed, varied and interactive environments offer multiple approaches to reach your goal. Sneak, climb, drive in various vehicles, or hide and creep your way to mission success!
[*] [b]On your mark[/b]: A modern user experience with precise and intuitive controls enables you to control the commandos with expert precision. Coordinate complex actions simultaneously to overcome heavily fortified targets.
[*] [b]Fight on all fronts[/b]: Play through more than 10 missions in historically authentic WWII environments, spanning from the barren Arctic to the African desert, with a range of core and voluntary objectives that will require your full tactical expertise.
[*] [b]There is no I in team[/b]: Take on missions with a friend in the 2-player cooperative multiplayer mode, either online or via local split-screen.
[/list]

notes.title: Commandos: Origins - A triumphant return
notes.content:
[h1]The Commandos series returns in 2024 with Commandos: Origins[/h1]

A new story from the classic real-time stealth tactics series is now in development

We are thrilled to announce that [b]Commandos, the iconic real-time stealth tactics game series, is making a triumphant return[/b] with "Commandos: Origins" in [b]2024[/b].

[previewyoutube=XHA9IAN3ZX8;full][/previewyoutube]

Commandos: Origins takes players back to World War II, where you can [b]see the original characters unite to form the legendary Commandos squad[/b]. Engage in close-quarters-combat with The Green Beret, Jack O’Hara, and take down Nazi soldiers with brutal strength and efficiency, or obliterate key tactical targets with The Sapper, a fearless firefighter turned demolitions expert.

A gripping storyline sets the stage for a thrilling adventure, filled with challenging missions and tactical stealth gameplay. With [b]over 10 missions across authentic historical locations[/b], spanning the icy landscapes of the Arctic to the scorching sands of the African desert, you'll find yourself facing varied scenarios and diverse objectives. Each mission offers a fresh and engaging experience that keeps players eagerly anticipating each new challenge.

The game offers an exhilarating and challenging real-time strategy gameplay experience allowing you to harness the unique abilities of the Commandos, master the art of stealth, to strike from the shadows, and vanish into the night before the enemy can react.

[b]Commandos: Origins is gearing up for a 2024 release[/b] and will be available on day one on Xbox Game Pass for console and PC and on Xbox Series X|S, Windows PC, and PlayStation 5.
